releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.14
releases.body:
# WeHavePhones 0.0.14

This alpha update lets you install, update and remove WoW from the Play screen without opening Battle.net. It also adds a touch layout editor, controller help in Battle.net, and lower CPU use after you enter the world.

Install over your existing version to keep your data.

## What's new

- **Install, update and remove games from Play.** Pick a game version on Play to **Install** it, or pick an installed one to **Play** or **Update**. **Verify** and **Uninstall** sit below **Open Battle.net**. They run through Battle.net's own installer without opening the Battle.net window, and a progress screen shows the download size, speed and time left. Uninstall keeps your add-ons.
- Play shows when the selected game has an update.
- **Account** on Play lists the WoW licenses Battle.net shows for the selected game, such as WoW1 and WoW2. Pick one and Play starts that license. Each game remembers its own choice.

releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.13
releases.body:
# WeHavePhones 0.0.13

This alpha update adds a floating game window and automatic Android keyboard support. It also reduces background CPU use and fixes several touch and graphics issues.

Install over your existing version to keep your data.

## What's new

- **Floating game window** is on by default. When you switch apps, the game can keep playing in Android's picture-in-picture window, capped at 20 FPS. Tap the window and use its expand button to return to full screen. You can turn it off in Settings. The background setting is now called **Keep running in background**.
- The Android keyboard opens when a WoW text field gains focus and closes when you finish typing. It stays closed while a hardware keyboard is connected.
- The game surface requests 60 Hz while you play, including during touch input, to reduce display power use on high-refresh-rate phones. WeHavePhones also cleans up leftover Wine processes shortly after a session ends.
- **Disable WoW voice chat** is on by default to reduce background CPU use. Turn it off in Settings if you use WoW's built-in voice chat.

## Touch controls

releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.12
releases.body:
# WeHavePhones 0.0.12

An alpha update fixing a controller regression in 0.0.11.

Install over your existing version to keep your data. **Do not uninstall first.**

## Touch controls

- The action wheel is now enabled by default on wide screens. Turn off **Menu → Touch controls → Action wheel** to use standard action bars. Existing saved choices are preserved.

## Fixes

- Moving the left stick on a controller no longer presses the D-pad too, so D-pad bindings in WoW only fire from the D-pad. This fixes a regression in 0.0.11 (#39).

## Validation

- All 14 host suites, the E2E runner self-test, ShellCheck, Ruff and Android Lint passed.
- Forever 1.60.1.70938 passed in the signed 0.0.12 RC on a Galaxy S23+. Controller UI persisted after an in-game exit and relaunch. World entry and jumping passed with default controls.
- Touch controls passed world entry, jumping, stick movement and camera turning. The wheel passed swipes in both directions, hub taps and casting Healing Touch from an existing slot.
- Settings were restored and controller UI returned after the touch tests. No new Android crash entries appeared.

releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.11
releases.body:
An alpha update with redesigned touch controls, lower graphics memory use and controller fixes.

Install over 0.0.10 to keep your data. **Do not uninstall first.** Setup → App update can install the published release for you.

## Major change to touch controls

The new touch action wheels have four rings of nine slots using WoW's Action Bars 6 to 8. Swipe around the hub or tap it to change rings, tap a slot to use it, and hold a slot to change it.

**Existing touch-control users may need to re-add their spells and items to the new wheels.**

![Redesigned touch controls with the action wheel](https://github.com/ashmerra/wehavephones/releases/download/v0.0.11/WeHavePhones-0.0.11-touch-controls.png)

## What's new

- Added 75%, 90% and 110% touch interface sizes. The movement stick, toolbar and other native touch controls now resize with the interface, at a gentler rate to keep them easy to tap.

releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.10
releases.body:
An alpha update focused on touch controls, launch reliability and addon apps.

Install over 0.0.9 to keep your data. **Do not uninstall first.** Setup → App update can install the published release for you.

## Changes

- Touch chat starts compact when you enter the world and expands when you use it. Its controls stay clear of page keys and the keyboard.
- The touch quest tracker sits below the player frame. Play-mode drags turn the character, and the current touch mode is easier to see.
- Fixed taps missing their target when the Android keyboard pans the game screen.
- Fixed an exited WoW process blocking the next launch.
- Disabled Wine audio codec drivers that delayed Battle.net startup. Previous controlled S23 measurements reached the Play button about six seconds sooner.
- Fixed WowUp hanging at its logo with a backport of Wine's large-message fix. Removed the obsolete WowUp app patch.
- Added automated game and addon app checks for contributors.

## Testing and limitations

- All 13 host check suites, the E2E runner self-test, ShellCheck, Ruff and Android Lint passed.

releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.9 gives the Commander X16's network card Zimodem's command-mode connections, so programs that open several connections at once, like Veranda's Gemini, Gopher, FTP and chat programs, now connect.

## What's new

- **Veranda's network programs connect.** The X16's network card now handles the Zimodem commands that [Veranda](https://github.com/veranda-x16/veranda) uses to keep several connections open at once. Its Gemini browser, Gopher client, FTP and chat programs can reach the internet from the emulator.
- **Secure connections.** Programs can now open encrypted (TLS) connections through the X16's network card, which Gemini and HTTPS need. As on the real card, the card does the encryption itself and doesn't check the server's certificate.

## Downloads

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.8
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.8 brings the Apple II to phones and tablets, turns the touch screen into the Commander X16's mouse and the NES Zapper, and fixes the picture being cut off on phones with a gesture bar.

## What's new

- **The Apple II on a phone or tablet.** Hold it upright for a keyboard: Android's own, with rows of Esc, Tab, Ctrl, the arrows and Delete above it, plus Open Apple and Closed Apple, which stay down while you touch them. Reset only presses once you've held it for half a second, so a stray tap won't reset the machine. Turn it sideways for a joystick: an analog stick that moves as far as you push it, and buttons 0 and 1. Move it, resize it or hide it from the pause menu, as with the other pads.
- **The touch screen is the X16's mouse.** Drag a finger on the picture to move the pointer, tap to click, tap with two fingers to right-click, and tap then hold to drag. It works in the app and in the browser, so mouse programs like the Veranda desktop work on a phone.
- **Tap to shoot with the Zapper.** In Zapper games like Duck Hunt, tap the picture where you want to shoot.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.7
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.7 brings the Commander X16 to phones and tablets, with a keyboard in portrait and a SNES pad in landscape, gives the X16 all its function keys and proper SNES controllers everywhere, and tidies up Android.

## What's new

- **The X16 on a phone or tablet.** Hold it upright for a keyboard: Android's own, with autocorrect and suggestions off, and rows of Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, the arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down and Delete/Insert above it. Ctrl and Alt are sticky, so Ctrl then C sends Ctrl+C; tap twice to hold them. Fn brings up F1 to F12. Turn it sideways for a SNES pad.
- **Hide controls.** The pause menu on a touch screen can hide the on-screen controls for the rest of the game, and show them again.
- **The X16's F-keys are its own.** On the X16, and on the other computers that use the whole keyboard (Skink and BASIC), F1 to F12 go to the machine, so programs like busterm get them all. Open Bus's own keys move behind Ctrl+Shift: Ctrl+Shift+F1 opens the menu, Ctrl+Shift+F2 saves a state, and so on.

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.6
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.6 lets you install the web version as an app that opens without the internet, and fixes a way to get stuck in a game on Android phones.

## What's new

- **Install the web version as an app.** At https://obus.tuxprint.com/, Chrome and Edge offer to install Open Bus with its own window and icon, and Settings → Library has an Install button where your browser supports it. On iPhone, use Share → Add to Home Screen.
- **The web version works offline.** Once it's been opened, it opens again with no internet connection. It still picks up updates whenever you're online.
- **Your games stay put in the browser.** When you first add a game, the page asks the browser not to clear your games when it runs low on space.

## Fixed

- **Stuck in the emulator's menu on an Android phone.** Pressing Select and Start together on the on-screen controls opened a menu the on-screen buttons couldn't work, so the only way out was to quit the game. On-screen Select and Start now go to the game. A gamepad's Select and Start still open the menu, and Back still pauses.

## Downloads

| System                 | File                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------- |

releases.name: Open Bus 0.4.5
releases.body:
Open Bus 0.4.5 makes the Android app work on phones and tablets, with on-screen controls for NES games, and keeps the Commander X16's clock on time.

## What's new

- **On-screen controls for NES games** on a phone or tablet with no gamepad: a D-pad, A and B, Select and Start. They hide when a gamepad connects and come back when it disconnects.
- **Move controls.** Drag each piece where you want it, make them bigger or smaller, turn the vibration off, or put B higher than A. Your layout is kept.
- **A pause menu for touch screens.** Back opens it: Resume, Save state, Load state, Reset, Move controls and Quit. Before this, there was no way out of a game on a phone without a gamepad.
- **The library on phones** stays clear of the status bar, navigation bar, camera cutout and on-screen keyboard. Games are always fullscreen.

releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 6

This QA build targets an intermittent early-boot hang reported on the Retroid Pocket 5.

The failed QA 5 diagnostic showed a live audio thread but no first presentation, native pipeline creation, scene target, or crash. The guest render thread stopped immediately after its first offscreen 2D captures.

QA 6 tightens the boot capture boundary:

- Only the four verified 2D vertex layouts and three supported primitive types are accepted.
- Individual and per-frame 2D payloads have conservative size limits.
- Invalid transient draw state is rejected before reading guest memory.
- The first twelve guest frames now log capture begin and completion markers.

Install QA 6 over the previous QA app, keep the System Driver selected, fully close the app between attempts, and test at least five launches. Attach diagnostics from any failed launch.

releases.body:
# Skate 3 Mobile v2.0.18 QA 5

This is an opt-in diagnostic build that installs over earlier **Skate 3 QA** builds and preserves QA app data.

## RP5 intermittent black-screen fix

QA 4 proved that the Retroid Pocket 5 can render the Quality profile's 1280x720 scene target, but testers reported that startup only succeeded roughly half the time.

The QA 4 profile copied Performance's visible feature settings, but one internal pipeline gate still used the profile number. Quality therefore compiled optional outline, spline, and shadow shader families even though those features were disabled. Cold and partially warmed shader caches could take different startup paths.

QA 5 fixes the mismatch:

- The 1280x720 Quality target remains enabled.
- The pipeline builder now follows the active lean-scene flag instead of assuming every Quality profile needs the full optional PSO set.
- Renderer installation applies the same defensive lean-feature guard.
- The startup log must report `lean Android set` for this QA Quality profile.
- Stable v2.0.17 and its update channel remain unchanged.

## RP5 test

1. Install QA 5 directly over QA 4.
2. Keep the System Driver selected.

releases.name: Eglantine Build 26/11/2026
releases.body:
Automatic daily build of `nx2-experimental` at `ed46267`.

## Changes since the previous daily build

39 commits since the 25/11 build. The big one is a rewrite of how ASTC textures are recompressed for Vulkan; the rest are game fixes, archive handling and recovery paths.

### Graphics — ASTC recompression is now a single pass ([#951](https://github.com/Eglantine-Community/Eglantine/pull/951))

Compressed textures no longer make a detour through a temporary RGBA8 image (decode → round trip through memory → encode). The BC1/BC3 blocks are written straight from the ASTC blocks the invocation touches, in one dispatch.

- **Much less memory moved** (`eb459b4118`). On Mario Kart World the old path held 236–851 MiB resident and pushed 74–657 MiB/s through it, over 33–180 transcodes a second. Now nothing but the blocks is written, so the decode image, its second dispatch, the barrier between them and the 64 MiB layer chunking are all gone.
- **Faster where it counts** (`3a1ce9cb1b`). An 8×8 footprint — the one these titles ship — used to decode each block up to four times over; it is one invocation per ASTC block now. A 1024×1024 level measures 2.1 ms instead of 5.2 ms on a GT 1030.

releases.name: v2.5.17 — Microsoft sign-in
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Microsoft sign-in no longer opens a blank white page** ([#3](https://github.com/FlameLaunchers/FlameLauncher-Android/issues/3)). Android's WebView puts `; wv` in its user agent, Microsoft reads that as an embedded browser and refuses the page — and what you get is not a message, it is an empty white screen. The marker is gone from the user agent now.

  Two more things the sign-in page needs were missing: cross-site cookies, which `login.live.com` relies on, and a `WebChromeClient`, without which the popups and dialogs the flow opens are silently dropped. The iOS build never hit any of this because WKWebView reports itself as Safari and handles those by default.
- **A sign-in page that fails to load now says why.** Main-frame errors were going nowhere, so a failure left the same white screen with nothing to report.

releases.name: v2.5.16 — Minecraft 26.4 snapshots
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Minecraft 26.4 snapshots start.** A version id like `26.4-snapshot-3` splits into `26` and `4-snapshot-3`, and reading that second part as a plain integer gave nothing — so 26.4 was treated as 26.0, missed the SDL and LWJGL 3.4.3 stack, and launched on LWJGL 3.3.6 instead. The game died immediately with `NoClassDefFoundError: org/lwjgl/sdl/SDLPlatform`; the cacio lines in the crash report were a consequence, not the cause. Version numbers are now read digit by digit, so snapshot, pre-release and rc suffixes no longer hide them, and five tests cover the shapes.
- Carries the previous fix as well: on Java 24 and newer the cacio java agent is skipped, because the `sun.misc.Unsafe` calls its `premain` depends on are refused there and a failing agent takes the VM with it.

releases.name: v2.5.15 — Minecraft 26.4 starts again
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Minecraft 26.4 (and anything else on Java 24 or newer) starts again.** The cacio setup loaded a java agent whose `premain` overwrites the AWT toolkit's static fields through `sun.misc.Unsafe` (`staticFieldBase`, `staticFieldOffset`, `putObject`). Those methods are refused from JDK 24 and gone in 26, and a failing agent takes the whole VM down with it — which surfaced as a cacio error at startup.

  The iOS build has always run the same cacio jars without that agent, on the same Java 25, using only `-Dawt.toolkit` and `-Xbootclasspath/a`. Android now does the same on Java 24+ and keeps the agent only for the older runtimes that still need it.

## Iron Lemon v0.3.0

**Lemon Online comes to Iron Lemon:** play a game's local multiplayer with your friends, wherever they are, in the same rooms as Lemon players. Plus recommended settings, Bramble support and the Lemon-Ade 0.0.9 driver. This is a preview release; Lemon stays the main app.

### Lemon Online
Lemon Online carries a game's **local wireless** play over the internet, so the game believes your friend's console is right next to yours, wherever they are. It works with any game that has a local wireless mode.

1. Open **Online** from the library, or from the in-game menu.
2. Create a room and share its code, or join one: with its code, from a friend's invite or from the public rooms.
3. Start the same game on every device and pick its **local wireless** mode (in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: **Wireless Play**, not **Online**).

releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.7.0

**Lemon Online is here:** play a game's local multiplayer with your friends, wherever they are. Plus recommended settings for each game, everything Bramble needs to show your games, and the Lemon-Ade 0.0.9 driver.

### Lemon Online
On a Switch, local wireless play only reaches the consoles in the same room. Lemon Online puts every player in one **room** on the internet and passes the game's local wireless traffic through it, so the game believes the other consoles are right next to it, even if your friend is on the other side of the world. It works with any game that has a local wireless mode.

1. Open **Online** from the library, or from the in-game menu.
2. Create a room and share its code, or join one: with its code, from a friend's invite or from the public rooms.
3. Start the same game on every device and pick its **local wireless** mode (in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: **Wireless Play**, not **Online**).

- **No account.** Each device gets a friend code. Nothing to sign up for.
- **Friends:** see who is online and what they play, invite them to your room. Accepting an invite opens the game.

## Lemon-Project v1.6.0

A round of fixes from your logs and reports, plus three things you asked for: a Nintendo button layout for physical controllers, frontends that bring a game's update and DLC along, and the Immediate GPU fences back as an option for advanced users.

### New
- **Button layout** (Settings → Controls): **Nintendo** swaps A↔B and X↔Y of your physical controller in games, so each button presses what a Switch has in its place. For handhelds and controllers with Xbox-style labels. Menus, hotkeys and button mapping still see the buttons as labelled.
- **Immediate GPU fences**, for advanced users (Graphics → Advanced → Synchronization, also per game). Off by default. When on, the game hears that the GPU is done as soon as the work is queued, instead of waiting for it to finish. It can raise FPS in some games (Link's Awakening, issue #53) and makes others flicker (Garfield, Dragon Ball), which is why it stays off by default.
- **Games opened from a frontend** (Argosy, Beacon, ES-DE…) now load the update, DLC and custom settings that sit beside them in the same folder (issue #52).
- The **firmware 23.5 home menu** starts.

# Winlator Mali Bionic 1.2.1

A fixes-and-polish update to 1.2.

## ⚠️ Reinstall Required!
Uninstall the old version and install 1.2.1 fresh. Back up your game saves first (Save Manager, or copy them out of your container). Containers made on 1.2 are not carried over.

## Fixes for 1.2 user reports
- Fixed a reboot on some MediaTek Mali phones (JM Mali).
- Fixed a crash when opening a shortcut.
- Fixed the controller binding editor.
- Fixed the stutter when holding D-pad right.
- Fixed File Manager not opening (it needed `libcdio.dll`), and File Manager hanging on x86_64 Wine (replaced with Bannerlator's newer `wfm.exe` / `winhandler.exe`).

## Graphics and performance
- **Fullscreen modes:** Fit, Stretch, Fill and Integer, plus screen alignment (Center, Top, Bottom half), set per container or per game and changeable live in Display & Session.
- **EGL stripes fixed:** CPU writes into the window buffer are flushed per X batch.
- **ZeroFG:** the default multiplier is capped at the display refresh rate (40 fps on a 60 Hz screen now gives 1.5x instead of 2x with dropped frames).
- **Gladio:** refuses OpenGL contexts above 3.3 again; libGL stripped of debug info (1.48 MB to 488 KB).

⚙️ Hybrid x86 FEXCore

What does it do?

Normally, disabling x86 Reduced Precision forces software emulation for all x86 code, which can significantly reduce performance.

releases.name: Castlevania port v0.5.0
releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

releases.name: Castlevania port v0.4.0
releases.body:
## Save report and update notices

Two new rows in the settings panel (swipe in from the right edge of the screen):

- **Save report** writes a folder `reports/<date>/` into your game folder: the log, a screenshot of the moment you opened the panel, the frame times of the last seconds and basic device information (model, Android version, memory). **Nothing is sent anywhere.** If something looks wrong, open an [issue](https://github.com/IamWilmar/castlevania-recomp/issues) and attach those files (have a look first: the log contains the names of your folders).
- **Update notices** (on by default): about eight seconds after the game starts, the app asks GitHub's public API which release is the latest. It is a single request, without an account, and nothing about you or your game is sent. If there is a newer version, a banner says so and *Get vX.Y.Z* opens its page. Switch it off in the panel (or create an empty file `sin_avisos_version` in the game folder) and the app makes no network request at all.
- Because of the update notices the app now has Android's **Internet** permission. It is used for that request only.

## Installing

releases.name: v0.2.0
releases.body:
## What's new

- **TV mode.** A new switch in the settings panel makes the game run as it does on a TV: the scene renders at 1344×756 instead of 896×504 and the game outputs a full 1080p, so the port no longer has to upscale it. It still holds 60 fps on the Flip 2 (GPU at ~78 %). The controller is then seen as a single wireless controller, which is what the game expects on a TV. The switch takes effect the next time you open the app; an empty `modo_tv` file in the game folder does the same.
- **Bluetooth and USB controllers fixed.** The Retroid's system re-creates every external controller with the device's own IDs, so the port took a DualSense (or any other pad) for the built-in one and, in Retro mode, swapped its buttons. Now the built-in controller is recognised by its name and every other controller is read by position, like on the game's original console: the bottom button is B, whatever mode the device is in.

## Installing

A native Android port of the console version of **Castlevania: Belmont's Curse** for the **Retroid Pocket 5** and the **Retroid Pocket Flip 2**, running from your own copy of the game.

Snap64 Recomp 1.1.8-test1 (test build for issue 39)
releases.body:
**This is a test build, not a release.** It is for [issue 39](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/issues/39): on a phone with an Exynos 2400, the Android app shows the same graphics message at every start once Anti-Aliasing is set to 8x. Everyone else should use [1.1.7](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/releases/tag/v1.1.7).

It is the code that will become 1.1.8, as it stands today. When the phone cannot make a picture buffer at the settings chosen, the port lowers a setting and asks for a restart. 1.1.7 only ever lowered Super Sampling, so with Super Sampling already at 1x nothing changed and every start ended the same way. This build lowers one setting each time: Super Sampling, then Anti-Aliasing, then Color Depth, then Render Scale. It never asks for an Anti-Aliasing level the phone does not offer, it remembers a level that failed, and the log names the levels the phone offers.

Install it over 1.1.7. Saves stay. If 1.1.7 left the phone stuck, the first start of this build should lower Anti-Aliasing to 4x by itself and get into the game. If it still stops, attach `snap64.log` from Internal storage > Snap64 to issue 39.

releases.name: Snap64 Recomp 1.1.7-test4 (test build for issue 36)
releases.body:
**This is a test build, not a release.** It is for the crash in [issue 36](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/issues/36): on an AYN Thor, the Android app closes as the game starts. Everyone else should use [1.1.7](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/releases/tag/v1.1.7).

It is [1.1.7-test3](https://github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/releases/tag/v1.1.7-test3) with a fix for the crash that build recorded. The Thor's graphics driver crashed at the end of the first drawing pass of the first frame. That pass held a reset of the renderer's timers, which Vulkan does not allow inside a drawing pass. The port's own clear of new picture buffers had left the pass open. Now the reset, and the two other steps Vulkan keeps outside a drawing pass, close an open pass first. The log says so once.

The crash record from test3 stays in. If the app still closes, open it once more, then attach `snap64.log` to issue 36. Saves stay.

releases.name: v0.1.8-alpha
releases.body:
### Changed

- The emulated display is 1080p by default (it was 2160p), in the launcher, `rps5e-cli run` and the test scripts: games that size their output to the display render a quarter of the pixels and the window scales the picture, which is much lighter on the GPU. 2160p (and 720p) stay selectable in the launcher's settings, per game, and with `--display-resolution` / `RPS5E_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION`. Games that do not ask for the display's resolution are shown a 2160p display as on the console.
- System functions answer as measured on a PS5 in a game process: a trylock of an adaptive mutex by its owner returns EINVAL (was EBUSY); `sceKernelAddAmprEvent` on a deleted or null event queue returns EBADF (was success); `sceSystemServiceReceiveEvent` with no event pending returns "no event" for any pointer and leaves the buffer untouched (it wrote an empty event first, and a null pointer was a parameter error); the `sceNetGetSockInfo` record carries the socket priority 0x10.
- `sceVideoOutSetFlipRate` checks the handle before the rate and accepts rate 3 (a flip every fourth vblank), as on a PS5.

releases.name: 0.1.7-alpha - 2026-11-13
releases.body:
### Fixed

- Ghost of Yōtei no longer freezes after its shaders are compiled (#3). Two causes:
  - Planning the resources of a shader walked the shader's whole value graph again for every word of every buffer descriptor; on this game's largest shaders that took minutes on the GPU command thread, with nothing submitted meanwhile. Each value is now walked once per shader.
  - A few compute shaders became SPIR-V modules of 2.7-3.2 million words that the GPU driver compiled for 15 minutes and more while the game waited (the driver keeps the result, so only the first run on a machine stalled). The largest is now 0.6 million words and builds in about 40 s on an RTX 5090, once; the results are the same, bit for bit (device tests over every buffer format, page-crossing elements and partial EXEC):

releases.body:
### Fixed

- Windows: controllers work out of the box. The release archive now carries `SDL3.dll`: the emulator loads SDL at run time and Windows has none of its own, so no controller was found ("SDL3 not available") unless the file was added by hand. The message for a missing library now says where to put it ([#4](https://github.com/keklick1337/rps5e/issues/4)).


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/keklick1337/rps5e/compare/v0.1.5-alpha...v0.1.6-alpha

releases.name: 1.0.5-alpha
releases.body:
### Changed

- The automatic choice of the recording thread (`RPS5E_GPU_RECORD_THREAD=auto`) no longer turns it off while the command interpreter also has to wait for room in its queue (`RPS5E_POLICY_FULL`). SILENT HILL: The Short Message's heavy room about 10 fps instead of 8; GTA V with `RPS5E_BDA=1` 47 fps instead of 42.
- `RPS5E_BDA=1` (experimental direct guest memory reads) no longer changes the default of `RPS5E_LABELS_AT_EOP`: with its old default (`1`) GTA V never left its start menu. GTA V's city in Performance mode with `RPS5E_BDA=1`: 47-48 fps against 37 without it; still off by default.
- The emulator's own small writes into GPU-watched guest memory (memcpy/memset inside one page, packets of the command-buffer builders) mark the page written before the store instead of taking a page fault (`RPS5E_PREMARK_SMALL`). GTA V's city in Performance mode: write faults per frame ~1550 → ~320; over the same stretch of the scene the frame rate rises by about 2.5 % (36.6 → 37.4 fps).

- Added a **Check for updates** button under **Settings > App**.

- The existing severe-heat protection remains enabled during gameplay.

releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.5-dev (versionCode 9).

### Changes

- Added native implementations of selected game, rendering, AI and container algorithms, with the original recompiled paths retained. Optimized guest-register handling, x87 calculations and indirect-call caches.
- Added Optimal (ARM64) and Exact (x86) execution modes. Exact selects the original recompiled algorithms; both modes run as ARM64 code.
- Reduced GLES state traffic between threads, draw preparation work and shader constant uploads, and improved shader program caching.
- Improved launcher operation progress, diagnostics and Play button feedback, with the amber UT3 palette.
- Added an optional 4 GB guest address space, enabled by default on 64-bit devices with at least 5 GiB of RAM.
- Fixed fingerprint sensors being mistaken for gamepads.
- Reduced APK size by stripping non-runtime library symbols while retaining the original library for offline profiling. Expanded regression tests and updated documentation.

### Requirements

Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4.1-dev (versionCode 8).

### Changes

- Improved CPU performance on PhysX Mod Pack maps with native fluid collision kernels, native pair removal and optimized x87 calculations.
- Added on-device HLSL compilation through vkd3d-shader, with shader caching and improved MojoShader compatibility for mod materials.
- Fixed touch aiming: holding Fire no longer blocks another finger's camera movement; dragging from Fire, secondary fire, Jump or Crouch also turns the camera.
- Made the crash monitor a launcher option, disabled by default, to avoid keeping its extra Android process running unless needed.
- Removed FSR3 frame generation. FSR1 spatial upscaling and FXAA remain available.

- Updated localized PhysX and audio setting descriptions.

Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4-dev.

### Changes

- Added an FPS counter with a frame-time graph and optional system information for every renderer.
- Added FSR1, FXAA, and FSR3.1 frame generation (DXVK, Android 12+; disabled by default).
- Added CPU-based PhysX effects and OpenAL Soft audio through AAudio with EAX 1–5 support.
- Added a maximum-graphics button and fixed persistence of the 3D rendering scale.
- Fixed terrain rendering in OpenGL ES, accelerated DXT decoding, and allowed unused texture mip levels to stream out.
- Improved GPU query handling in GLES and DXVK, including on PowerVR devices.
- Fixed ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion on shared storage on Pixel devices.
- Added a “Firing or aiming” gyroscope mode and persistent crash reports with a separate error window.

### Installation and limitations

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; frame generation requires Android 12+. Frame generation may cause HUD artifacts and adds GPU and memory overhead. A stable 60 FPS at maximum graphics settings is not guaranteed.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.3-dev
releases.body:
The third release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 improves GLES performance, text editing and graphics cache handling.

### Changes

- Added a dedicated GLES render thread with automatic CPU core selection. Streamed draw uploads, asynchronous query polling and shader program prelinking reduce work on the game thread.
- Added driver-aware graphics cache maintenance: GLES program binaries are invalidated after driver changes, and DXVK keeps the current and newest other pipeline cache for each driver.
- Fixed DXVK scaled vertex formats with a shader fallback for drivers that need it.
- Replaced keyboard-only text entry with an Android editing dialog for game fields, console commands and chat. Existing text can be corrected or cleared; cancellation preserves it, and original character filters remain in effect.
- Added separate weapon-button swipe settings and expanded the in-game Android settings to nine languages: English, Russian, Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian and Polish.
- Improved launcher texture status and fixed texture handling, audio and FSINCOS translation. Expanded regression tests and rendering diagnostics.

### Requirements

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 0.2-dev
releases.body:
The second release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 adds optional texture conversion, more flexible touch controls, OpenSpy compatibility and save/profile fixes.

### Changes

- Added optional ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion in the launcher, including games played directly from stored ZIP archives. Original packages are retained; runtime DXT decoding remains available for cache misses and mods.
- Added a touch layout editor to move, resize and hide individual controls. Hold the on-screen Pause button to open it; a short tap opens the original pause menu.
- Expanded touch settings with a fixed joystick, weapon tap/swipe selection, separate weapon bar/wheel sizes, control visibility, movement while holding primary fire and horizontal gyro reversal.
- Added OpenSpy service and authentication compatibility, and fixed a registry-call crash during online play.
- Prevented startup defaults from overwriting saved profiles and campaign progress before sign-in. Fixed creation of save directories beneath virtual ZIP folders.

releases.name: recomp-launcher 0.3.0
releases.body:
### Added
- The installer shows its version (the game's tag, or the short commit for a
  build off a branch) in the window's corner and title, and on start asks
  GitHub for the game's newest release: a newer one gets a download button.
  Offline it says nothing.
- `game.files` takes globs: `*.iso` makes a folder holding a disc image the
  game, for a title whose setup takes an image rather than an install.
- `installer.yml` takes `platforms` (default `windows linux macos`), so a
  Windows-only game doesn't publish installers that can't build it.
- A `game.files` entry may be alternatives, `a|b`: `HOVER.EXE|hover*.zip` is
  the game's folder or a folder holding a zip of it.

- The Windows installer carries version info and a manifest, and a release
  has `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so antivirus heuristics and players can check it.
- A log of why the installer stopped (`%APPDATA%\recomp-launcher\launcher.log`
  on Windows), and an error box instead of the window vanishing.

### Fixed
- On Windows a step line after a blank line was glued to the line before it
  (ConPTY skips the blank line with a cursor move), so the bar missed that step.

releases.name: hakuX 1.3.0
releases.body:
Xbox Live through Insignia, and game fixes.

### Xbox Live
- **Insignia** — Settings → Network → Connection → Xbox Live: Insignia connects the console to Insignia, the revival of the original Xbox Live: Live games sign in, find matches and play online. If your Internet provider blocks Insignia's DNS server, point it at a computer running insigniaDNS instead
- **Xbox Live setup** — Settings → Network → Xbox Live setup walks you through it, one step at a time: the connection, the Xbox dashboard, registering the console with Insignia's Setup Assistant (downloaded for you), then making or recovering your account in the dashboard
- **Dashboard** — the library's Dashboard button (top left) starts the Xbox dashboard from the console's hard disk, where Xbox Live accounts are made and recovered. The first time, it installs the dashboard from a zip of its files (dashboard 5960) that you provide: hakuX doesn't include one
- **Title updates** — a game's Xbox Live update, once downloaded, starts with the game. Forza Motorsport's 60 and 120 fps mods cover its update too

### Games
- **Fable: The Lost Chapters** — the hero's face and arms are no longer black or noise

releases.name: hakuX 1.2.0
releases.body:
System link, stability and compatibility improvements.

### Network
- **System link over your network** — Settings → Network → System link → LAN: hakuX devices on the same Wi-Fi network find each other as Xbox consoles on a LAN do. Devices the network's broadcasts don't reach, on another subnet or a VPN such as ZeroTier or Tailscale, are added by address under Other consoles
- **XLink Kai** — system link over the Internet through an XLink Kai engine running on a computer on your network; its web page picks the game's arena
- **Console identity** — each console has its own serial number, network address and online key. A device whose hard disk was copied from another one offers to make itself a new identity, since two consoles with one identity can't see each other


### Games
- **Sega GT 2002** — the cars have their paint, reflections and sun highlights
- **Doom 3** — no longer crashes as its main menu loads
- **Fatal Frame II** — starts and reads its disc in the order it asks for
- **AirForce Delta Storm** — answers the controller and the on-screen controls (it ignored all input)
- **Silent Hill 2** — no longer crashes when it loads a room

releases.name: hakuX 1.1.0
releases.body:
GPUs beyond Adreno (experimental).

### GPUs
- **Mali, Xclipse and PowerVR (experimental)** — hakuX runs on GPUs other than Adreno: features they lack are replaced (BC and 4444 textures decoded up front, standard border colours, the push block in a buffer, D32S8 depth), and known driver bugs are worked around (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`). Burnout 3 and Mercenaries run cleanly on a Pixel 8 (Mali-G715)
- **Vulkan 1.1 drivers** — GPUs whose drivers stop at Vulkan 1.1 (Valhall Mali on older or vendor-capped drivers, Qualcomm's own older drivers, early Xclipse, PowerVR BXM) run through a compatibility layer (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/compat.c`)
- **Older GPUs without descriptor indexing (experimental)** — Bifrost Mali (G71, G72, G76, G52) and PowerVR Rogue: each draw binds its own textures, and depth is clamped in the shader where the GPU can't
- **Adreno** — unchanged: every replacement is off where the GPU has the feature.

### App
- **GPU driver** — a screen of its own (Settings → GPU driver): the system driver and the stored packages in one list, with their versions and authors. Packages are checked when added and can be deleted (deleting the one in use goes back to the system driver)

releases.name: hakuX 1.0.0
releases.body:
A new core replaces xemu's QEMU-based one.

### New core
- **CPU** — the Xbox's x86 code runs on a FEX JIT (FEXCore fork), and the Xbox kernel is reimplemented natively (`native/kernel`): no QEMU
- **GPU** — the NV2A push buffer is decoded into Vulkan (HLE, `hw/xbox/hle`). Custom drivers (Turnip) load through adrenotools; driver-specific workarounds are quirks (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`, `debug.hakux.quirks`)
- **Audio** — the MCPX APU runs on the core's own services (`native/dev/apu`), out through AAudio
- **Savestates** — per game, in slots, with the hard disk's files
- **Mods and cheats** — per game, from `mods/` (library long-press "Mods & cheats"): XBE patches and replaced disc files; 60 and 120 fps mods for 13 games (`mods/README.md`, generators in `tools/mods`)
- **Controllers** — each physical controller routed to a player with its own mapping; the on-screen controller adds to player 1

### New features
- **Updates** — hakuX looks for a newer release on GitHub when it starts and on demand (Settings → Updates); one found shows its notes and installs from there
- **Frontends** — a game launched from ES-DE or another frontend returns to it when it closes

releases.body:
# SeedlessDS 1.1 正式版

版本名为 `1.1`，版本号为 `153`。本次同时发布原包名替换版、共存版、对应源码及 SHA-256 校验文件。两版均关闭 Android 调试标志，正式版本号与发布文件名均不含 debug，测试控制面板关闭。

## 本次改进

- 修复后台存档提前完成时，完成状态被模拟线程覆盖，导致后续快速存档和读档一直被忽略的问题。
- 减少存读档结束后的多余槽位查询、成就附加档读取和目录扫描，成就校验改为流式 SHA-256。
- 拆分即时存档、游戏电池存档和其它文件的访问锁，避免后台慢存档连带阻塞游戏文件读取。后台存档线程降低优先级。
- 防止并发慢查询重新发布已失效的目录列表，修复日志时间格式化的并发访问。
- 在应用私有目录保留有大小上限的近期存读档记录，便于追查偶发卡顿。
- 保留 SoundTouch 原声音高加速、低延迟音频恢复修复，以及按 RP Duo 上下屏实际画面尺寸适配的柔和颗粒、柔和颗粒＋和 Nova 磷光点滤镜。

## 安装包选择

| 文件 | Android 包名 | 安装方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `seedless-ds-1.1-coexist.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app.debug` | 可直接更新本分支旧共存版，也可与官方版共存 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-replacement.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app` | 原包名替换版 |
| `seedless-ds-fork-1.1-src.zip` | — | 两版对应的完整源码与构建配置 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-SHA256.txt` | — | 安装包和源码校验值 |

共存版按用户选择保留历史包名中的 `.debug`，以支持覆盖更新，应用本身已关闭调试。两版均沿用本分支旧签名。

替换版与官方版签名不同。首次换用替换版，请先导出存档与配置，再卸载官方版并安装。直接覆盖官方版会因签名不匹配而失败。两个包名的数据各自独立，切换使用时需导入存档。

两版均支持 ARM64，最低 Android 5.0。证书 SHA-256 为 `99e2395bd7c458a577e6bc4f4c7237a7474cb20a178fad07313c2778a7943165`，沿用仓库随源公开测试签名。

## 验证范围

- 两种正式构建各 128 项应用测试通过，完成构建、Lint、包名和签名检查，并核对 `debuggable=false`、`testOnly=false` 及 `BuildConfig.DEBUG=false`。两版的应用资源和原生库一致。
- 原生回归覆盖 21 类存档故障、280 轮重复存读档及请求交错。

- 修复后台存档提前完成时，完成状态被模拟线程覆盖，导致后续快速存档和读档一直被忽略的问题。
- 减少存读档结束后的多余槽位查询、成就附加档读取和目录扫描，成就校验改为流式 SHA-256。
- 拆分即时存档、游戏电池存档和其它文件的访问锁，避免后台慢存档连带阻塞游戏文件读取。后台存档线程降低优先级。
- 防止并发慢查询重新发布已失效的目录列表，修复日志时间格式化的并发访问。
- 在应用私有目录保留有大小上限的近期存读档记录，便于追查偶发卡顿。
- 保留 SoundTouch 原声音高加速、低延迟音频恢复修复，以及按 RP Duo 上下屏实际画面尺寸适配的柔和颗粒、柔和颗粒＋和 Nova 磷光点滤镜。

## 安装包选择

| 文件 | Android 包名 | 安装方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `seedless-ds-1.1-coexist.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app.debug` | 可直接更新本分支旧共存版，也可与官方版共存 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-replacement.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app` | 原包名替换版 |
| `seedless-ds-fork-1.1-src.zip` | — | 两版对应的完整源码与构建配置 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-SHA256.txt` | — | 安装包和源码校验值 |

共存版按用户选择保留历史包名中的 `.debug`，以支持覆盖更新，应用本身已关闭调试。两版均沿用本分支旧签名。

替换版与官方版签名不同。首次换用替换版，请先导出存档与配置，再卸载官方版并安装。直接覆盖官方版会因签名不匹配而失败。两个包名的数据各自独立，切换使用时需导入存档。

两版均支持 ARM64，最低 Android 5.0。证书 SHA-256 为 `99e2395bd7c458a577e6bc4f4c7237a7474cb20a178fad07313c2778a7943165`，沿用仓库随源公开测试签名。

## 验证范围

- 两种正式构建各 128 项应用测试通过，完成构建、Lint、包名和签名检查，并核对 `debuggable=false`、`testOnly=false` 及 `BuildConfig.DEBUG=false`。两版的应用资源和原生库一致。
- 原生回归覆盖 21 类存档故障、280 轮重复存读档及请求交错。

releases.name: 358/2 Days for Android: 0.1.5 beta 14
releases.body:
Fourteenth beta of KINGDOM HEARTS 358/2 Days for Android on **[khdays-port 0.1.5](https://github.com/Yokimitsuro/khdays-port/releases/tag/v0.1.5)**, Yokimitsuro's native PC port that this Android version follows. All the credit for the port itself goes there.

Coming from an earlier beta? The game offers this update itself on the title screen, or install the APK below by hand; your game, HD files and saves are kept.

## What's new since beta 13

- **No more flicker in the camera's crossfades on Mali graphics chips** (AYANEO Pocket Air Mini and other Mali devices). In a cutscene's crossfade between two camera shots, some pictures showed the new shot with blocks of the old one in it, and the fade went back and forth. The graphics driver ran two steps of the picture in the wrong order; they are now done in a way it keeps in order.
- **No pause in the middle of a cutscene when a KH2 model with moving cloth first appears** (with the HD PACK). The first such model's cloth used to be prepared on the spot, about a sixth of a second; all of them are now prepared in the background while the title shows.

Coming from an earlier beta? The game offers this update itself on the title screen, or install the APK below by hand; your game, HD files and saves are kept.

## What's new since beta 12

- **Sharper tutorial pages and lower-screen menus on one screen.** When the lower screen is shown big over the whole picture (a tutorial page, the load menu, the world list, a mission's page), it is now drawn at the size it is shown at, and a tutorial page's text is drawn sharp on its own. Before, it was drawn at the lower screen's own resolution and stretched, so the text came out soft.
- **Far-away enemies move every frame.** From khdays-port's development branch: Days only updated enemies far from the camera every other frame, which made them stutter on a smooth picture.

releases.name: 358/2 Days for Android: 0.1.5 beta 12
releases.body:
Twelfth beta of KINGDOM HEARTS 358/2 Days for Android on **[khdays-port 0.1.5](https://github.com/Yokimitsuro/khdays-port/releases/tag/v0.1.5)**, Yokimitsuro's native PC port that this Android version follows. All the credit for the port itself goes there.

Coming from an earlier beta? The game offers this update itself on the title screen, or install the APK below by hand; your game, HD files and saves are kept.

## What's new since beta 11

A beta about speed with the HD pack's KH2 models.

- **Scenes with the KH2 character models are no longer slow.** A KH2 model with a coat made the whole 3D picture take a slow path. On a Mali-G57 tablet the scene after Day 7 ran at 16-22 pictures a second; now 51-60. Stronger devices gain too in close-ups.
- **Enhanced character shadows cost much less.** With the setting on, an AYN Thor went from 93 to 62 pictures a second in the Grey Area; now 86.
- **A frozen picture on Mali devices is recovered from.** When the graphics driver stopped answering, the picture stood still for good while the game went on. The game now notices and carries on after a short hitch, and one of the two moments where it happened is gone.

## What's new since beta 10

A small beta about starting the game.

- **Much faster starts on some devices.** The graphics card's programs are now kept between starts instead of being made again every time. On the AYN Odin (Adreno 630) the screen stayed black for one to four minutes at every start; now it is about 3 seconds. Other devices start a little faster too.

## New since v2.1.6 (last stable)

- **Steam ISO manual export** — Steam ISO files (`<Game Name>.iso` to `Downloads/front end/`) are no longer written automatically on every game list load. They are now written on demand via the **FileDownload** (↓) button in the My Games top bar, preventing unnecessary writes and duplicate file churn.

- **Game name sanitization** — Game names are sanitized before being used in MediaStore queries and ISO file creation (colons and other illegal filename characters are replaced), fixing a crash/failure when Steam game names contain colons or other special characters.

---

## Full Feature Set

**Core**
- No root required — uses Android's Storage Access Framework (SAF) for secure folder access.
- Single data/ grant — one SAF permission at `<package>/data` covers components, virtual containers, and shadercache simultaneously.
- Multi-app support — automatically detects all installed GameHub variants side by side.

releases.name: v2.1.9-pre
releases.body:
Move Steam ISO export from automatic (every load) to a manual button.

The download arrow (⬇) button appears in the My Games top bar when an app is selected and Steam games are loaded. Tapping it writes/updates the ISOs for all Steam games on demand.

Navigation is now instant — no more SteamRepository.fetch() + MediaStore operations firing silently on every tab visit.

releases.name: v2.1.8-pre
releases.body:
Fix Counter-Strike: Source (and any game with : in the name) creating a new ISO every launch.

**Root cause:** Steam game names with colons (e.g. `Counter-Strike: Source`) get stored in MediaStore with the colon replaced by `_`. The existence check queried with the original name (colon), found nothing, and inserted again — MediaStore then auto-renamed the new file to `Counter-Strike_ Source (1).iso`, `(2).iso`, etc.

**Fix:** Sanitize filename chars `[/\\:*?"<>|]` → `_` before any MediaStore query or insert, so both sides always agree on the name.

releases.name: v2.1.7-pre
releases.body:
Fix duplicate ISO files in Downloads/front end/ on every app launch.

**Root cause:** The old code called MediaStore delete() then insert() each launch. On Android, delete() removes the catalog entry but not the physical file — so insert() would see the file already on disk and auto-rename it to `Counter-Strike_ Source (1).iso`, `(2).iso`, etc.

**Fix:** Query first. If the ISO already exists, skip writing it entirely. No duplicates.

# Skyrim for Android 0.30.6

APK: `Skyrim-0.30.6.apk` (arm64-v8a, Android 9+, Vulkan 1.1).

## New
- "Disable end-of-frame image space (post-processing)" option. It does the same as the TEOFIS console command at every launch. It fixes the black world map and solid-colour underwater screen, but it also turns off all end-of-frame post-processing (tonemapping, bloom, colour grading and depth of field), so the game looks more naturally lit.
- "Asynchronous rendering" option. It's off by default and when it's on, shaders compile on background threads. New effects may pop in for a frame or two instead of causing a hitch. 

## Fixed
- Shader caching is removed. The DXVK state cache rebuilt every saved pipeline on 5 extra threads at startup, which took CPU away from the game's main thread and caused crashes on Mali devices. Nothing is cached between launches now, and the game runs better overall.
- Traps triggering freezes was due to failed lookups with vertex optimization. The function has been turned off for now.
- Audio in other languages - the decoder was reading each WMA bitstream but with the wrong block-size config. Should be working now.

# WinLite v1.4.0

## Overview
A release focused on rendering smoothness, a new X11 server and Steam support.

---

## 🎮 BETA - Steam
- Steam client support added.

---

## 🖥️ X11 server (rewritten in Rust)
The built-in X server has been rewritten from scratch in Rust and now covers much more of the X11 protocol.

**What you get**
- **Stability.** Memory-safe code removes a whole class of crashes and hangs.
- **Better game and launcher compatibility.** Newer screen-configuration (RANDR 1.2) and rendering extensions are supported, so Wine, launchers and games see a more complete environment.
- **Proper mouse cursors.** System cursors are drawn from a built-in cursor set, and colored/semi-transparent and animated cursors are supported.
- **Better frame pacing.** Frame presentation is synchronized with the real display refresh rate and with fences, which gives the renderer and the FPS limiter an accurate clock to work from.
- **Faster window drawing.** The shared frame buffer is locked once per operation instead of repeatedly, and more drawing requests (lines, rectangles, area clears) are handled directly.

天玑 / MediaTek X11 专版 · 合成器测试版

本版基于 1.2.0 天玑 X11 分支，**唯一改动是打开 KWin 合成器**，用于真机验证桌面特效（窗口晃动、魔灯等）能否真正生效。

#### 本版改了什么

此前每次启动桌面会话时，脚本都会把 `kwinrc` 强制改写为：

```ini
[Compositing]
Enabled=false
Backend=QPainter
```

这正是「在系统设置里勾了窗口晃动 / 魔灯，晃了半天毫无反应」的直接原因——**合成器关着，KWin 会静默忽略全部桌面特效**。

本版改为：

```ini
[Compositing]
Enabled=true
Backend=OpenGL
GLCore=false
LatencyPolicy=Low
WindowsBlockCompositing=false
```

后端固定为 **OpenGL（硬件）**，不使用纯软件 QPainter 后端；LLVM 软件渲染（llvmpipe / swrast）在部署时仍会被删除。

#### ⚠️ 这是未经验证的测试版，请只用于测试

发布者手上没有天玑真机，**本版没有在任何天玑设备上跑过**。请把预期放低。

已知的关键疑点（在我的机器上实测发现，属于**设备无关**的问题）：

1. **guest rootfs 内缺少 `virpipe_dri.so`**。逐个列出 rootfs 中全部 Mesa DRI 驱动后确认：有 `virtio_gpu_dri.so`、`zink_dri.so`、`panfrost_dri.so`、`mediatek_dri.so`，**但没有 `virpipe_dri.so`**——而这正是 VirGL 的 guest 端驱动。会话脚本仍在强制 `GALLIUM_DRIVER=virpipe` + `VTEST_SOCKET=/tmp/.virgl_test`，即**指向一个不存在的驱动**。若真机因此拿不到 GL 上下文，合成器就起不来。
2. **相反方向的证据**：发布者在高通测试机上开启 OpenGL 合成后桌面全黑，日志为 `MESA: error: ZINK: vkGetCalibratedTimestampsEXT failed (VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY)`。但那条日志同时说明 **KWin 当时确实拿到了 GL 上下文**（走的是 Zink）。这与第 1 点互相矛盾，怀疑 KWin 走 EGL 入口、Qt 走 GLX 入口，两者对 `GALLIUM_DRIVER` 的处理不同。

> **The project is still being prepared.** The source code is not public yet — it will be open-sourced in [NixPort/nixport](https://github.com/zFitness/nixport) once the release is ready. What you get here today is the documentation plus a runnable APK.

**Install:** download `nixport.apk` from this release and install it on an ARM64 Android phone (Android 9 / API 28 or newer). The APK ships the Linux environment inside it and unpacks it on first run.

If the app is already installed, update from inside the app (Home). Note that this build is signed with a different key than the CI-published ones, so it may require uninstalling the previous build first.

**SHA-256 of `nixport.apk`:**
`9541187e23d823f1e883ad002c002093791437fc740544e370addbd9c1208817`

**Size:** 281,440,841 bytes

`nixport.json` next to the APK carries the same metadata (commit, build time, size, SHA-256) and is what the in-app updater reads.

**Nixport v1.2.304-alpha** — a test build for people who want to try it early.

> Published by hand: built and signed with the same key as v1.1.299-alpha and
> v1.0.267-alpha (upgrades install over them without uninstalling).

## Changelog (since v1.1.299-alpha)

### Gamepads

- **Single-player pad model** (replaces v1.1's player slots): exactly one physical
  pad feeds the game at a time. The pad you touch takes over automatically
  (last-active wins); the session drawer offers "use this pad" to pin a choice for
  the session. The effective pad and the on-screen controls merge into one player.
- **Fix: intermittent directional input**. After opening a menu or losing focus,
  sticks / D-pad / triggers now reach the game immediately at their current position —
  no more "only X works in the load screen" or "the first press does nothing".
  The old "stay blocked until centered" gate is gone (keys only).
- Rumble now always lands on the effective pad (Xbox-protocol pads don't expose
  motors to Android — enable "phone vibration" as the fallback).
- On-screen stale-state fix: a closed overlay can no longer pin the virtual stick
  over the physical one.

Second beta pre-release of **AoI Native** (`io.github.p1r4n351.hwaoi`) for **Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment** (`04003F40232DE000`, update `v196608`, Nintendo Switch 2 Edition). **This is a developer/tester beta, not a finished end-user release.**

## Read this first

- **No game files, keys, firmware, shaders, or saves are included.** You must supply your own legally obtained Switch 2 `.nup` / dump of `04003F40232DE000` (`v196608`).
- **On-device setup & shader compilation bundled (`NX_PACK_ENGINE=native`):** This release embeds the native packer and SPIR-V translator (`libpython3.14.so`, `libnxpack.so`, `libdmsh_xlate.so`, `libSPIRV-Tools-shared.so`, `libzbicdec.so`, `libcra.so`). Pre-built `dmsh_vk.lib` archives prepared with `scripts/pack_android.py` also drop directly into the pack folder.
- **Target hardware:** 16 GB **AYN Thor** (`QCS8550` / Adreno 740, Android 13 SDK 33, 1080p top screen + `1240x1080` secondary `Display 4`) with Mesa `Turnip`.

releases.name: v1.1 — Movies in sync / Vídeos sincronizados
releases.body:
## The 3rd Birthday for Android — v1.1

### Fixed
- **Movies (cutscenes) are smooth and in sync with their audio.** The phone's video decoder runs in parallel and sometimes answers a few milliseconds late; each late picture was lost and pushed the rest of the movie one frame later, so the picture ended up seconds behind the sound. Now the app waits briefly for each picture and catches up if one is late. The end of a movie is no longer cut short either.
  Measured on a Moto G200: opening movie 4140 of 4141 frames, picture 138.2 s vs audio 138.1 s (before, a 35 s movie lost 91 frames and ended ~3 s behind).
- Future app updates no longer ask you to rebuild the game when nothing it needs has changed.

### Updating from v1.0
Install the new APK over the old one (your saves stay). **This one time** the app asks to rebuild the game (**Update the game**, ~10 minutes, uses the ISO you already imported). Later updates skip this unless really needed.

### New install

releases.body:
## The 3rd Birthday for Android — v1.0

First public release. **No computer needed**: install the APK, tap **Choose ISO**, pick your own copy of the game (US version, `ULUS10567`), and the phone builds the game once (about 10 minutes on a Moto G200). Then just play.

**This APK contains no Square Enix code or data.** You need your own copy of the game (a dump of your UMD).

### How to install
1. Download **`the-3rd-birthday-android-v1.0.apk`** below and install it (allow installing from this source).
2. Open the app, allow notifications, tap **Choose ISO** and pick your `.iso`.
3. Wait for **"Ready! The game is built."** and tap **Play**.

Step-by-step guide: [TUTORIAL_EN.md](https://github.com/onederson/the-3rd-birthday-recomp-android/blob/main/TUTORIAL_EN.md)

### Highlights
- Builds the game on the phone from your ISO (bundled Zig compiler). Keeps going with the app minimized and resumes if Android closes the app.
- Internal resolution 1x–4x and 30–144 FPS, live.
- Touch controls with a layout editor (swipe the right side to turn the camera, double tap to reset it), physical controllers, native settings menu on Back.

### Requirements
